topics.title: Research & publication
topics.summary: Under section 5.11 of the Responsible Conduct of Research Policy (MPF1318) and active University guidance, researchers must document DAT use, disclose tools in outputs, and obtain privacy/security/ethics approvals. For graduate research theses, AI editing is strictly restricted to minor language and clarity support under Australian Standards for Editing Practice, with supervisor AI review requiring explicit written candidate consent.
topics.scope: Subject-level assessment guidelines; Student Academic Integrity Policy (MPF1310); Student Appeals Policy (MPF1323); Responsible Conduct of Research Policy (MPF1318 cl 5.11); Open-book exams advice; Canvas LMS privacy notice.

claims.text: Under section 5.11 of the Responsible Conduct of Research Policy (MPF1318) and University guidance, research personnel must document digital assistance tool use, disclose DAT use to collaborators and in outputs (including theses), and obtain all required privacy, security, and ethics approvals.

evidence.quote:
In line with section 5.11 of the Responsible Conduct of Research Policy, research personnel are responsible for assuring the integrity of their research produced with the assistance of digital assistance tools, including but not limited to artificial intelligence (AI) tools. Research personnel must:
Document the use of a digital assistance tool (DAT) in their research process
Disclose the use of a DAT to research partners, collaborators and in research outputs, including but not limited to publications and theses
evidence.title: Responsible Use of AI in Research (Policy and Guidance)
evidence.location: Section: Responsible Conduct of Research Policy cl. 5.11 obligations; extracted text lines 36-38

evidence.quote: Ensure all necessary approvals are obtained to use the DAT, including but not limited to a Privacy Impact Assessment, Information Security Risk Assessment, or ethical review and approval where applicable.
evidence.title: Responsible Use of AI in Research (Policy and Guidance)
evidence.location: Section: Approvals for DAT Use; extracted text lines 39-39

claims.text: For graduate researchers and research theses, digital assistance and GenAI use is strictly limited to minor editorial support (language, clarity, spelling, grammar) under the Australian Standards for Editing Practice; substantial redrafting is prohibited and supervisor AI review requires explicit written permission.

evidence.quote: Whether rephrasing text moves beyond minor editing assistance, and therefore impacts the integrity of the research output, depends on whether the rephrasing is beyond that acceptable according to the Australian Standards for Editing Practice. These standards limit editing to language and expression (clarity, grammar, spelling), completeness and consistency. Substantial redrafting of whole paragraphs or larger sections, or translating a substantial body of text into English, falls outside those limits.
evidence.title: Responsible Use of AI in Research (Policy and Guidance)
evidence.location: Section: Australian Standards for Editing Practice and thesis limits; extracted text lines 84-84

evidence.quote:
A specific case is material provided to supervisors by their graduate researchers. These candidates own their text so it can only be uploaded into an AI with their explicit permission and with a clear statement of the purpose for which it is being uploaded. This also applies to co-authored material such as drafts of papers.
Thus, if a supervisor plans to use AI to provide feedback on written material, they must obtain the candidate’s permission to do so, and it is a reasonable expectation on the part of the candidate that this permission be recorded in writing.
evidence.title: Responsible Use of AI in Research (Policy and Guidance)
evidence.location: Section: Supervisor AI Review Permission; extracted text lines 80-81

additionalTopics.title: Academic integrity & procedures
additionalTopics.summary: Under MPF1310, unauthorised or undisclosed technology use in assessable work constitutes academic misconduct. Poor Academic Practice is managed educatively by Subject Coordinators, distinct from formal Faculty Level 1 and Serious Level 2 misconduct. Turnitin AI detection reports serve as an investigative prompt rather than proof, students have the right to provide drafts and explanations in exploratory discussions, and MPF1323 establishes a 20-university-business-day appeal window.
additionalTopics.scope: Subject-level assessment guidelines; Student Academic Integrity Policy (MPF1310); Student Appeals Policy (MPF1323); Responsible Conduct of Research Policy (MPF1318 cl 5.11); Open-book exams advice; Canvas LMS privacy notice.

evidence.quote: It’s important your students realise that if an assessment task does not permit the use of such tools, or if they use such tools in the preparation of an assessment submission without acknowledgement, this constitutes academic misconduct under cl. 4.13 of the Student Academic Integrity Policy (MPF1310).

evidence.location: Section: University policies in relation to Generative AI; extracted text lines 57-57

claims.text: The University of Melbourne academic misconduct framework explicitly categorizes unauthorized or undisclosed use of technology (including GenAI) as a breach type under academic integrity procedures.

evidence.quote:
Breach types
Plagiarism
Unauthorised re-use of previous work (self plagiarism)
Breach of examination or assessment rules or directions
Falsification or misrepresentation of data
Unauthorised or undisclosed use of technology (incl. GenAI)
evidence.title: Student Academic Integrity: What Changed in 2025? (MPF1310 Implementation)
evidence.location: Section: Managing Suspected Academic Misconduct - Breach Types; extracted text lines 128-133

claims.text: Poor academic practice refers to minor and unintentional departures managed educatively by Subject Coordinators, and is explicitly distinct from academic misconduct.

evidence.quote:
Poor academic practice refers to minor and unintentional departures from accepted scholarly conventions or failures to comply with assessment guidelines. Poor academic practice incidents are characterised by inexperience, lack of student knowledge, or poor academic skills, and does not compromise the purpose and/or integrity of the assessment.
Importantly, poor academic practice is not academic misconduct, may be treated as an assessment matter and managed within the marking and assessment guidelines set by the Board of Examiners for the subject.
evidence.title: Student Academic Integrity: What Changed in 2025? (MPF1310 Implementation)
evidence.location: Section: Poor Academic Practice Definition and Management; extracted text lines 66-67

claims.text: A high AI score in Turnitin's writing detection report is not proof of misconduct and does not on its own constitute grounds for making an allegation of academic misconduct.

evidence.quote: A high AI score in Turnitin’s writing detection report is not proof that academic misconduct has taken place (any more than would be the case when using the more familiar similarity report tool to flag potential plagiarism).  It does not, on its own, constitute grounds for making an allegation of academic misconduct.
evidence.title: Generative AI in T&L at the University of Melbourne (Melbourne CSHE)
evidence.location: Section: Turnitin Writing Detection Guidance; extracted text lines 37-37

claims.text: Turnitin AI detection results serve only as a prompt for further investigation; if suspected, students may be invited to explain their work and provide drafts or notes in an exploratory discussion.

evidence.quote:
As with the similarity report generated by Turnitin, the result of the AI writing detector tool is a prompt for further investigation.
Should there be a suspicion that part or all of your submitted assessment has been produced using generative AI, you may be asked to explain your essay and argument (how you developed the argument, what sources you used, how you reached the conclusion you did), or to provide drafts or notes of early versions of the assessment.
evidence.title: Advice for Students Regarding Turnitin and AI Writing Detection
evidence.location: Section: Advice for Students Regarding Turnitin - Prompt for investigation; extracted text lines 15-16
